newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil's toy output to rise 15 pct next year.
newsitem.headline: Brazil's toy output to rise 15 pct next year.

text.p: Brazil's toy production is expected to rise by 15 percent in 1997 to 166 million units due to an increase in productivity and lower imports, said Brazil's Association of Toy Manufacturers (Abrinq).

"These figures are still bellow the 202 million toys we produced in 1994, our annual record," said Synesio da Costa, Abrinq's president, noting that sales revenues are likely to rise by five percent next year to $630 million.
Earlier this year, Brazil rose import tariffs on toys by 70 percent to give time to the domestic toy industry to restructure and become more competitive.
The government's move will force toy imports to fall to $100 million in 1996 from $164 million last year, Costa said.

Costa said the industry would take five years to have the same 1994 production levels, adding that the sector plans to invest 112 million reais ($108.4 million) in 1997 to expand and modernize plants and marketing.
He said the industry will invest to increase production scale and allow toy prices to fall by seven percent next year.

"Our plan is to put toy prices down so we can sell them to the poor families," Costa said. He noted the average of new toys per child a year in Brazil is only eight, while in developed countries this average can reach 20.
